children.translated_text: The <s>Vajracchedikā</s> (Diamond Cutter), the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) in Three Hundred [Lines].

body.text: | namo bhagavatyā āryaprajñāpāramitāyai ||
body.translated_text: Homage to the noble <s>Bhagavatī Ārya-Prajñāpāramitā</s> (the Blessed Lady, the Noble Perfection of Wisdom).

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane' nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārthaṃ trayodaśabhirbhikṣuśataiḥ saṃbahulaiśca bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ | atha khalu bhagavān pūrvāhṇakālasamaye nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya śrāvastīṃ mahānagarīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat | atha khalu bhagavān śrāvastīṃ mahānagarīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātapratikrāntaḥ pātracīvaraṃ pratiśāmya pādau prakṣālya nyaṣīdatprajñapta evāsane paryaṅkamābhujya ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhīṃ smṛtimupasthāpya | atha khalu saṃbahulā bhikṣavo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāman | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirobhirabhivandya bhagavantaṃ triṣpradakṣiṇīkṛtya ekānte nyaṣīdan || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s> (Jeta's Grove), in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great assembly of monks — thirteen hundred monks — and with many <s>bodhisattvas</s>, great beings (<s>mahāsattvas</s>). Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at the time of the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having walked through the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms, having eaten his meal, returned from his almsround after the meal, put away his bowl and robe, washed his feet, and sat down on the seat prepared for him, crossing his legs, holding his body upright, and establishing mindfulness before him. Then many monks approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, circumambulated him three times, and sat down to one side. || 1 ||

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayenāyuṣmān subhutistasyāmeva parṣadi saṃnipatito 'bhūtsaṃniṣaṇṇaḥ | atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirutthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - āścaryaṃ bhagavan, paramāścaryaṃ sugata, yāvadeva tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anuparigṛhītāḥ parameṇānugraheṇa | āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvadeva tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ parīnditāḥ paramayā parīndanayā | tatkathaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvayānasaṃprasthitena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā sthātavyaṃ kathaṃ pratipattavyaṃ kathaṃ cittaṃ pragrahītavyam?
body.translated_text: At that time, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> was present in that assembly, seated. Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: "It is wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s>! It is most wonderful, <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), how much the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One), the Perfectly Enlightened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), has sustained the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the great beings, with the highest sustenance! It is wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s>, how much the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has entrusted the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the great beings, with the highest entrustment! How then, <s>Bhagavān</s>, should a son or daughter of good family who has set out on the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle stand? How should they practice? How should they control the mind?"

body.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - sādhu sādhu subhūte, evametatsubhūte, evametadyathā vadasi | anuparigṛhītāstathāgatena bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ parameṇānugraheṇa | parīnditāstathāgatena bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ paramayā parīndanayā | tena hi subhūte śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te - yathā bodhisattvayānasaṃprasthitena sthātavyaṃ yathā pratipattavyaṃ yathā cittaṃ pragrahītavyam | evaṃ bhagavan ityāyuṣyān subhūtirbhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt ||2 ||
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Well said, well said, <s>Subhūti</s>! So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is, as you say. The <s>Tathāgata</s> has sustained the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the great beings, with the highest sustenance. The <s>Tathāgata</s> has entrusted the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the great beings, with the highest entrustment. Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, listen, and attend well and carefully — I shall speak to you: how one who has set out on the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle should stand, how one should practice, how one should control the mind." "So be it, <s>Bhagavān</s>," the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. || 2 ||

body.text: bhagavānasyaitadavocat - iha subhūte bodhisattvayānasaṃprasthitenaiva cittamutpādayitavyam - yāvantaḥ subhūte sattvāḥ sattvadhātau sattvasaṃgraheṇa saṃgṛhītā aṇḍajā vā jarāyujā vā saṃsvedajā vā aupapādukā vā rūpiṇo vā arūpiṇo vā saṃjñino vā asaṃjñino vā naivasaṃjñino nāsaṃjñino vā, yāvān kaścitsattvadhātuḥ prajñapyamānaḥ prajñapyate, te ca mayā sarve 'nupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāpayitavyāḥ | evamaparimāṇānapi sattvān parinirvāpya na kaścitsattvaḥ parinirvāpito bhavati | tatkasya hetoḥ? sacetsubhūte bodhisattvasya sattvasaṃjñā pravarteta, na sa bodhisattva iti vaktavyaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? na sa subhūte bodhisattvo vaktavyo yasya sattvasaṃjñā pravarteta, jīvasaṃjñā vā pudgalasaṃjñā va pravarteta || 3 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this: "Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, one who has set out on the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle should produce this thought: 'However many beings there are in the realm of beings (<s>sattvadhātu</s>), comprehended under the category of beings — whether egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, or spontaneously born; whether having form or formless; whether having perception, without perception, or neither with perception nor without perception; whatever realm of beings is designated as such — all of them I should lead to <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>parinirvāṇa</s>), into the realm of <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>anupadhiśeṣa nirvāṇadhātu</s>).' Yet even having led immeasurable beings to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, no being whatsoever has been led to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Why is that? If, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> were to have the notion of a being (<s>sattvasaṃjñā</s>), he should not be called a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Why is that? He should not be called a <s>bodhisattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, in whom the notion of a being, the notion of a life-force (<s>jīvasaṃjñā</s>), or the notion of a person (<s>pudgalasaṃjñā</s>) would arise." || 3 ||

children.translated_text: <s>Vajr</s>, <s>Vaidya</s> 76

children.text: ) api tu khalu punaḥ subhute na bodhisattvena vastupratiṣṭhitena dānaṃ dātavyam, na kvacitpratiṣṭhitena dānaṃ dātavyam | na rūpapratiṣṭhitena dānaṃ dātavyam | na śabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmeṣu pratiṣṭhitena dānaṃ dātavyam | evaṃ hi sūbhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena dānaṃ dātavyaṃ yathā na nimittasaṃjñāyāmapi pratitiṣṭhet | tatkasya hetoḥ? yaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo 'pratiṣṭhito dānaṃ dadāti, tasya subhūte puṇyaskandhasya na sukaraṃ pramāṇāmudgrahītum | tatkiṃ manyase subhūte sukaraṃ pūrvasyāṃ diśi ākāśasya pramāṇamudgrahītum? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | bhagavānāha - evaṃ dakṣiṇapaścimottarāsu adha ūrdhvaṃ digvidikṣu samantāddaśasu dikṣu sukaramākāśasya pramāṇamudgrahītum? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | bhagavānāha - evameva subhūte yo bodhisattvo 'pratiṣṭhito dānaṃ dadāti, tasya subhūte puṇyaskandhasya na sukaraṃ pramāṇamudgrahītum | evaṃ hi subhūte bodhisattvayānasaṃprasthitena dānaṃ dātavyaṃ yathā na nimittasaṃjñāyāmapi pratitiṣṭhet || 4 ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> should not give a gift while abiding in [any] object; a gift should not be given while abiding in anything whatsoever. A gift should not be given while abiding in form. A gift should not be given while abiding in sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental objects (<s>dharma</s>). For thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, should a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> give a gift — in such a way that one does not abide even in the perception of a sign (<s>nimitta</s>). For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the heap of merit (<s>puṇyaskandha</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who gives a gift without abiding [in anything] is not easy to measure. What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is it easy to measure the extent of space in the eastern direction? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, <s>Bhagavan</s>. The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: Likewise, is it easy to measure the extent of space in the southern, western, and northern directions, below, above, in the intermediate directions, in all ten directions? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, <s>Bhagavan</s>. The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: Just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, the heap of merit of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who gives a gift without abiding [in anything] is not easy to measure. For thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, should one who has set out on the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle give a gift — in such a way that one does not abide even in the perception of a sign. || 4 ||

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte lakṣaṇasaṃpadā tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | na lakṣaṇasaṃpadā tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? yā sā bhagavan lakṣaṇasaṃpattathāgatena bhāṣitā saivālakṣaṇasaṃpat | evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat yāvatsubhūte lakṣaṇasaṃpat tāvanmṛṣā, yāvadalakṣaṇasaṃpat tāvanna mṛṣeti hi lakṣaṇālakṣaṇatastathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ || 5 ||
body.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Should the <s>Tathāgata</s> be seen through the perfection of [physical] marks (<s>lakṣaṇasaṃpad</s>)? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, <s>Bhagavan</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s> should not be seen through the perfection of marks. For what reason? Because that perfection of marks spoken of by the <s>Bhagavan</s> is itself the perfection of non-marks (<s>alakṣaṇasaṃpad</s>). When this was said, the <s>Bhagavan</s> said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: Insofar as there is the perfection of marks, <s>Subhūti</s>, so far it is false; insofar as there is the perfection of non-marks, so far it is not false. Thus, through marks and non-marks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is to be seen. || 5 ||

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - asti bhagavan | kecitsattvā bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani paścime kāle paścime samaye paścimāyāṃ pañcaśatyāṃ saddharmavipralopakāle vartamāne, ye imeṣvevaṃrūpeṣu sūtrāntapadeṣu bhāṣyamāṇeṣu bhūtasaṃjñāmutpādayiṣyanti | api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ paścime kāle paścime samaye paścimāyāṃ pañcaśatyāṃ saddharmavipralope vartamāne guṇavantaḥ śīlavantaḥ prajñāvantaśca bhaviṣyanti, ye imeṣvevaṃrūpeṣu sūtrāntapadeṣu bhāṣyamāṇeṣu bhūtasaṃjñāmutpāadayiṣyanti | na khalu punaste subhūte bodhisattvā mahāsattvā ekabuddhaparyupāsitā bhaviṣyanti, naikabuddhāvaropitakuśalamūlā bhaviṣyanti | api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte anekabuddhaśatasahasraparyupāsitā anekabuddhaśatasahasrāvaropitakuśalamūlāste bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bhaviṣyanti, ye imeṣvevaṃrūpeṣu sūtrāntapadeṣu bhāṣyamāṇeṣu ekacittaprasādamapi pratilapsyante | jñātāste subhūte tathāgatena buddhajñānena, dṛṣṭāste subhūte tathāgatena buddhacakṣuṣā, buddhāste subhūte tathāgatena | sarve te subhūte aprameyamasaṃkhyeyaṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyanti pratigrahīṣyanti | tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi subhūte teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmātmasaṃjñā pravartate, na sattvasaṃjñā, na jīvasaṃjñā, na pudgalasaṃjñā pravartate | nāpi teṣāṃ subhūte bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ dharmasaṃjñā pravartate | evaṃ nādharmasaṃjñā | nāpi teṣāṃ subhūte saṃjñā nāsaṃjñā pravartate | tatkasya hetoḥ? sacetsubhūte teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ dharmasaṃjñā pravarteta, sa eva teṣāmātmagrāho bhavet, sattvagrāho jīvagrāhaḥ pudgalagrāho bhavet | sacedadharmasaṃjñā pravarteta, sa eva teṣāmātmagrāho bhavet, sattvagrāho (

children.translated_text: [Vajr, Vaidya p. 77]

children.text: ) jīvagrāhaḥ pudgalagrāha iti | tatkasya hetoḥ? na khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena dharma udgrahītavyo nādharmaḥ | tasmādiyaṃ tathāgatena saṃdhāya vāgbhāṣitā - kolopamaṃ dharmaparyāyamājānadbhidharmā eva prahātavyāḥ prāgevādharmā iti || 6 ||
children.translated_text: grasping at a living being (<s>jīvagrāha</s>), or grasping at a person (<s>pudgalagrāha</s>). For what reason? Indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should not seize upon either <s>dharma</s> or non-<s>dharma</s>. Therefore this statement was spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> with a hidden intention: 'Those who understand the <s>dharma</s>-discourse to be like a raft should abandon even <s>dharmas</s>, how much more so non-<s>dharmas</s>.' || 6 ||

body.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavan</s>: Will there be, <s>Bhagavan</s>, any beings in the future time, in the last period, in the last epoch, in the last five hundred [years] when the destruction of the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma-vipralopa</s>) is taking place, who, when <s>sūtra</s> passages of this kind are being spoken, will generate the perception of truth? — Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, there will be in the future time <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, in the last period, in the last epoch, in the last five hundred [years] when the destruction of the true <s>Dharma</s> is taking place, who will be endowed with virtues, endowed with moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), and endowed with wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), who, when <s>sūtra</s> passages of this kind are being spoken, will generate the perception of truth. Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> will not have attended upon only one <s>Buddha</s>, nor will they have planted roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) under only one <s>Buddha</s>. Rather, <s>Subhūti</s>, those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> will have attended upon many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> and will have planted roots of merit under many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> — they who, when <s>sūtra</s> passages of this kind are being spoken, will attain even a single moment of serene faith (<s>ekacittaprasāda</s>). They are known, <s>Subhūti</s>, by the <s>Tathāgata</s> through <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge; they are seen, <s>Subhūti</s>, by the <s>Tathāgata</s> through the <s>Buddha</s>-eye; they are understood, <s>Subhūti</s>, by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. All of them, <s>Subhūti</s>, will beget and receive an immeasurable, incalculable heap of merit. For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the perception of self (<s>ātmasaṃjñā</s>) does not arise in those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, nor the perception of a being (<s>sattvasaṃjñā</s>), nor the perception of a soul (<s>jīvasaṃjñā</s>), nor the perception of a person (<s>pudgalasaṃjñā</s>). Nor, <s>Subhūti</s>, does the perception of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmasaṃjñā</s>) arise in those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>. Likewise, neither the perception of non-<s>dharma</s> (<s>adharmasaṃjñā</s>). Nor, <s>Subhūti</s>, does [any] perception or non-perception arise in them. For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, if the perception of <s>dharma</s> were to arise in those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, that itself would be their grasping of self (<s>ātmagrāha</s>), grasping of a being (<s>sattvagrāha</s>), grasping of a soul (<s>jīvagrāha</s>), grasping of a person (<s>pudgalagrāha</s>). And if the perception of non-<s>dharma</s> were to arise, that itself would be their grasping of self, grasping of a being —

body.text: punaraparaṃ bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte, asti sa kaściddharmo yastathāgatenānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirityabhisaṃbuddhaḥ, kaścidvā dharmastathāgatena deśitaḥ? evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - yathāhaṃ bhagavan bhagavato bhāṣitasyārthamājānāmi, nāsti sa kaściddharmo yastathāgatena anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirityabhisaṃbuddhaḥ, nāsti dharmo yastathāgatena deśitaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? yo 'sau tathāgatena dharmo 'bhisaṃbuddho deśito vā, agrāhyaḥ so 'nabhilapyaḥ | na sa dharmo nādharmaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? asaṃskṛtaprabhāvitā hyāryapudgalāḥ || 7 ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — is there any <s>dharma</s> that has been fully awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect enlightenment), or any <s>dharma</s> that has been taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s>?' Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'As I understand the meaning of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, there is no <s>dharma</s> that has been fully awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, nor is there a <s>dharma</s> that has been taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For what reason? That <s>dharma</s> which was awakened to or taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s> is ungraspable and inexpressible. It is neither <s>dharma</s> nor non-<s>dharma</s>. For what reason? Because the noble persons (<s>āryapudgala</s>) are distinguished by the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>).' || 7 ||

body.text: bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yaḥ kaścitkulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ saptaratnaparipūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tathāgatebhyo 'rhadbhayaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyo dānaṃ dadyāt, api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyāt | subhūtirāha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyāt | tatkasya hetoḥ? yo 'sau bhagavan puṇyaskandhastathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ, askandhaḥ sa tathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ | tasmāttathāgato bhāṣate - puṇyaskandhaḥ puṇyaskandha iti | bhagavānāha - yaśca khalu punaḥ subhūte kulaputro vā kuladuhitā va imaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ saptaratnaparipūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tathāgatebhyo 'rhadbhyaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyo dānaṃ dadyāt, yaśca ito dharmaparyāyādantaśaścatuṣpādikāmapi gāthāmudgṛhya parebhyo vistareṇa deśayet saṃprakāśayet, ayameva tatonidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyādaprameyasaṃkhyeyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? atonirjātā hi subhūte tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ, atonirjātāśca buddhā bhagavantaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? buddhadharmā buddhadharmā iti subhūte abuddhadharmāścaiva te tathāgatena bhāṣitāḥ | tenocyante buddhadharmā iti || 8 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — if some son or daughter of a good family were to fill this trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>) with the seven precious things and give it as a gift to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the perfectly enlightened ones, would that son or daughter of a good family produce a great heap of merit (<s>puṇyaskandha</s>) on that account?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'A great one, <s>Bhagavān</s>; a great one, <s>Sugata</s> — that son or daughter of a good family would produce a great heap of merit on that account. For what reason? That which the <s>Bhagavān</s> has called a heap of merit, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared to be a non-heap. Therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s> speaks of "a heap of merit, a heap of merit."' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'And yet, <s>Subhūti</s>, if a son or daughter of a good family were to fill this trichiliocosm with the seven precious things and give it as a gift to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the perfectly enlightened ones, and if [another person] were to take from this <s>dharma</s>-discourse even just a single verse of four lines and teach and illuminate it to others in detail — this [latter] one would on that account produce a far greater heap of merit, immeasurable and incalculable. For what reason? Because from this, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the perfectly enlightened ones, has arisen; and from this the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> have arisen. For what reason? <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s> — these have been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be non-<s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. Therefore they are called <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>.' || 8 ||

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu srotaāpannasyaivaṃ bhavati - mayā srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptamiti? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | na srotaāpannasyaivaṃ bhavati - mayā srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptamiti | tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi sa bhagavan kaṃciddharmamāpannaḥ, tenocyate srotaāpanna iti | na rūpamāpanno na śabdān na gandhān na rasān na spraṣṭavyān dharmānāpannaḥ | tenocyate srotaāpanna iti | sacedbhagavan srotaāpannasyaivaṃ bhavet - mayā srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptamiti, sa eva tasyātmagrāho bhavet, sattvagrāho jīvagrāhaḥ pudgalagrāho bhavediti ||
body.translated_text: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — does a <s>srotaāpanna</s> (stream-enterer) think thus: "The fruit of stream-entry has been attained by me"?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. A <s>srotaāpanna</s> does not think thus: "The fruit of stream-entry has been attained by me." For what reason? Because, <s>Bhagavān</s>, he has not entered upon any <s>dharma</s> — therefore he is called a "stream-enterer." He has not entered upon form, nor sounds, nor smells, nor tastes, nor tangibles, nor <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore he is called a <s>srotaāpanna</s>. If, <s>Bhagavān</s>, a <s>srotaāpanna</s> were to think thus — "The fruit of stream-entry has been attained by me" — that would indeed be grasping at a self (<s>ātmagrāha</s>), grasping at a being (<s>sattvagrāha</s>), grasping at a living being (<s>jīvagrāha</s>), and grasping at a person (<s>pudgalagrāha</s>).'

body.text: bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu sakṛdāgāmina evaṃ bhavati - mayā sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptamiti? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | sa sakṛdāgāmina evaṃ bhavati - mayā (

children.translated_text: [Vajr, Vaidya p. 78]

children.text: ) sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptamiti | tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi sa kaściddharmo yaḥ sakṛdāgāmitvamāpannaḥ | tenocyate sakṛdāgāmīti ||
children.translated_text: the fruit of once-returning has been attained." For what reason? Because there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that has entered upon the state of once-returning. Therefore he is called a <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>.' ||

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — does a <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returner) think thus: "The fruit of once-returning has been attained by me"?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. A <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> does not think thus: "By me

body.text: bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu anāgāmina evaṃ bhavati - mayānāgāmiphalaṃ prāptamiti? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | na anāgāmina evaṃ bhavati - mayā anāgāmiphalaṃ prāptamiti | tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi sa bhagavan kaściddharmo yo 'nāgāmitvamāpannaḥ | tenocyate anāgāmīti ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — does the thought occur to a Non-returner (<s>Anāgāmin</s>): 'The fruit of Non-returning has been attained by me'? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. The thought does not occur to a Non-returner: 'The fruit of Non-returning has been attained by me.' For what reason? Because, <s>Bhagavān</s>, there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that has entered the state of Non-returning. Therefore one is called a Non-returner (<s>Anāgāmin</s>).

body.text: bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu arhata evaṃ bhavati - mayā arhattvaṃ prāptamiti? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | nārhata evaṃ bhavati - mayā arhattvaṃ prāptamiti | tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi sa bhagavan kaściddharmo yo 'rhannāma | tenocyate - arhanniti | sacedbhagavan arhata evaṃ bhavet - mayā arhattvaṃ prāptamiti, sa eva tasyātmagrāho bhavet, sattvagrāho jīvagrāhaḥ pudgalagrāho bhavet | tatkasya hetoḥ? ahamasmi bhagavaṃstathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena araṇāvihāriṇāmagryo nirdiṣṭaḥ | ahamasmi bhagavan arhan vītarāgaḥ | na ca me bhagavannevaṃ bhavati - arhannasmyahaṃ vītarāga iti | sacenmama bhagavannevaṃ bhavet - mayā arhattvaṃ prāptamiti, na māṃ tathāgato vyākariṣyadaraṇāvihāriṇāmagryaḥ subhūtiḥ kulaputro na kvacidviharati, tenocyate araṇāvihārī araṇāvihārīti || 9 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — does the thought occur to an <s>Arhat</s>: '<s>Arhatship</s> has been attained by me'? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. The thought does not occur to an <s>Arhat</s>: '<s>Arhatship</s> has been attained by me.' For what reason? Because, <s>Bhagavān</s>, there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that is called an <s>Arhat</s>. Therefore one is called an <s>Arhat</s>. If, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the thought were to occur to an <s>Arhat</s>, 'Arhatship has been attained by me,' that itself would be his grasping at a self (<s>ātmagrāha</s>), grasping at a being (<s>sattvagrāha</s>), grasping at a life-force (<s>jīvagrāha</s>), grasping at a person (<s>pudgalagrāha</s>). For what reason? I, <s>Bhagavān</s>, have been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), as the foremost of those who dwell in peace (<s>araṇāvihārin</s>). I, <s>Bhagavān</s>, am an <s>Arhat</s>, free from passion (<s>vītarāga</s>). Yet, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the thought does not occur to me: 'I am an <s>Arhat</s>, free from passion.' If, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the thought were to occur to me, '<s>Arhatship</s> has been attained by me,' then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would not have declared: '<s>Subhūti</s>, the son of good family, the foremost of those who dwell in peace, does not dwell anywhere at all — therefore he is called one who dwells in peace, one who dwells in peace.' // 9 //

body.text: bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte - asti sa kaściddharmo yastathāgatena dīpaṃkarasya tathāgatasyārhata - samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntikādudgṛhītaḥ? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | nāsti sa kaściddharmo yastathāgatena dīpaṃkarasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntikādudgṛhītaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — is there any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that was received by the <s>Tathāgata</s> from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>)? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. There is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that was received by the <s>Tathāgata</s> from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

body.text: bhagavānāha - yaḥ kaścitsubhūte bodhisattva evaṃ vadet - ahaṃ kṣetravyūhān niṣpādayiṣyāmīti, sa vitathaṃ vadet | tatkasya hetoḥ? kṣetravyūhāḥ kṣetravyūhā iti subhūte avyūhāste tathāgatena bhāṣitāḥ | tenocyante kṣetravyūhā iti | tasmāttarhi subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena evamapratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamutpādayitavyaṃ yanna kvacitpratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam | na rūpapratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamutpādayitavyaṃ na śabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmapratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam | tadyathāpi nāma subhūte puruṣo bhavedupetakāyo mahākāyo yattasyaivaṃ rūpa ātmabhāvaḥ syāt tadyathāpi nāma sumeruḥ parvatarājaḥ | tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu mahān sa ātmabhāvo bhavet? subhūtirāha - mahān sa bhagavān, mahān sugata sa ātmabhāvo bhavet | tatkasya hetoḥ? ātmabhāva ātmabhāva iti bhagavan na bhāvaḥ sa tathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ | tenocyata ātmabhāva iti | na hi bhagavan sa bhāvo nābhāvaḥ | tenocyate ātmabhāva iti || 10 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: If any <s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, were to say, 'I shall bring about the adornment of [Buddha-]fields (<s>kṣetravyūha</s>),' he would speak falsely. For what reason? The adornments of fields, <s>Subhūti</s>, have been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be non-adornments (<s>avyūha</s>). Therefore they are called adornments of fields. Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should produce a thought that is unsupported (<s>apratiṣṭhita</s>) — a thought that is not supported anywhere. One should not produce a thought supported by form (<s>rūpa</s>); one should not produce a thought supported by sound, smell, taste, touch, or <s>dharmas</s>. Suppose, <s>Subhūti</s>, there were a person endowed with a body, a great body, such that his physical form (<s>ātmabhāva</s>) were like <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains. What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — would that physical form be great? <s>Subhūti</s> said: Great indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>; great indeed, <s>Sugata</s>, would that physical form be. For what reason? Physical form, physical form — that, <s>Bhagavān</s>, has been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be non-being (<s>na bhāva</s>). Therefore it is called a physical form. For, <s>Bhagavān</s>, it is neither being nor non-being. Therefore it is called a physical form. // 10 //

body.text: bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte - yāvatyo gaṅgāyāṃ mahānadyāṃ vālukāstāvatya eva gaṅgānadyo bhaveyuḥ? tāsu yā vālukāḥ, api nu tā bahvayo bhaveyuḥ? subhūtirāha - tā eva tāvadbhagavan bahvayo gaṅgānadyo bhaveyuḥ, prāgeva yāstāsu gaṅgānadīṣu vālukāḥ | bhagavānāha - (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajracchedikā</s>, <s>Vaidya</s> [edition, page] 79

children.text: ) ārocayāmi te subhūte, prativedayāmi te | yāvatyastāsu gaṅgānadīṣu vālukā bhaveyustāvato lokadhātūn kaścideva strī vā puruṣo vā saptaratnaparipurṇaṃ kṛtvā tathāgatebhyo 'rhadbhayaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyo dānaṃ dadyāt, tat kiṃ manyase subhūte - api nu sā strī vā puruṣo vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyāt? subhūtirāha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata strī vā puruṣo vā tatonidānaṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyādaprameyamasaṃkhyeyam | bhagavānāha - yaśca khalu punaḥ subhūte strī vā puruṣo vā tāvato lokadhātūn saptaratnaparipūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tathāgatebhyo 'rhadbhayaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyo dānaṃ dadyāt, yaśca kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā ito dharmaparyāyādantaśaścatuṣpādikāmapi gāthāmudgṛhya parebhyo deśayet saṃprakāśayet, ayameva tatonidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyādaprameyamasaṃkhyeyam || 11 ||
children.translated_text: I declare to you, <s>Subhūti</s>, I announce to you: if some woman or man were to fill as many world-systems (<s>lokadhātu</s>) as there are grains of sand in those <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers with the seven precious things and give them as a gift (<s>dāna</s>) to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>)—what do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, would that woman or man thereby produce a great heap of merit (<s>puṇyaskandha</s>)? <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Great indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Great indeed, <s>Sugata</s>! That woman or man would thereby produce a heap of merit, immeasurable and incalculable." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "But if, <s>Subhūti</s>, some woman or man were to fill that many world-systems with the seven precious things and give them as a gift to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones, and if a son or daughter of good family (<s>kulaputra</s>, <s>kuladuhitā</s>) were to take up from this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on dharma) even a single verse of four lines (<s>catuṣpādikā gāthā</s>) and teach and illuminate it for others—this one would thereby produce a far greater heap of merit, immeasurable and incalculable." || 11 ||

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — if there were as many <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers as there are grains of sand in the great river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and [if one considered] all the grains of sand in those [rivers] — would those grains of sand be many? <s>Subhūti</s> said: Those <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers alone, <s>Bhagavān</s>, would be many indeed — how much more so the grains of sand in those <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers! The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: api tu khalu punaḥ subhute yasmin pṛthivīpradeśe ito dharmaparyāyādantaśaścatuṣpādikāmapi gāthāmudgṛhya bhāṣyeta vā saṃprakāśyeta vā, sa pṛthivīpradeśaścaityabhūto bhavet sadevamānuṣāsurasya lokasya, kaḥ punarvādo ye imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sakalasamāptaṃ dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti | parameṇa te subhūte āścaryeṇa samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti | tasmiṃśca subhūte pṛthivīpradeśe śāstā viharatyanyatarānyataro vā vijñagurusthānīyaḥ || 12 ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, whatever spot of earth where from this discourse on <s>dharma</s> even a single verse of four lines is taken up, spoken, or illuminated—that spot of earth becomes a shrine (<s>caitya</s>) for the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. How much more so those who will preserve, recite, master this entire <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, and illuminate it in detail for others! They, <s>Subhūti</s>, will be endowed with the highest wonder. And in that spot of earth, <s>Subhūti</s>, the Teacher dwells, or one or another who stands in the place of a learned master. || 12 ||

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - ko nāma ayaṃ bhagavan dharmaparyāyaḥ, kathaṃ cainaṃ dhārayāmi? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - prajñāpāramitā nāmāyaṃ subhūte dharmaparyāyaḥ | evaṃ cainaṃ dhāraya | tatkasya hetoḥ? yaiva subhūte prajñāpāramitā tathāgatena bhāṣitā, saiva apāramitā tathāgatena bhāṣitā | tenocyate prajñāpāramiteti ||
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "What is the name of this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on dharma), <s>Bhagavān</s>? And how should I preserve it?" Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "This <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, is called the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). Thus should you preserve it. Why is that? That very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, which has been spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>—that itself has been spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as a non-perfection (<s>apāramitā</s>). Therefore it is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>." ||

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte - api nu asti sa kaściddharmo yastathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | nāsti sa kaściddharmo yastathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—is there any <s>dharma</s> that has been spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. There is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that has been spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>." ||

body.text: bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte - yāvat trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau pṛthivīrajaḥ kaccit, tadbahu bhavet? subhūtirāha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata pṛthivīrajo bhavet | tatkasya hetoḥ? yattadbhagavan pṛthivīrajastathāgatena bhāṣitam, arajastadbhagavaṃstathāgatena bhāṣitam | tenocyate pṛthivīraja iti | yo 'pyasau lokadhātustathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ, adhātuḥ sa tathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ | tenocyate lokadhāturiti ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—the dust particles (<s>pṛthivīrajas</s>) in the great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>), would they be many?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Many indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Many indeed, <s>Sugata</s>! Those dust particles would be many. Why is that? Those dust particles, <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s>—as non-particles have they been spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore they are called 'dust particles.' And that world-system spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s>—as a non-system (<s>adhātu</s>) has it been spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore it is called 'a world-system.'" ||

body.text: bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaistathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho draṣṭavyaḥ? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaistathāgato 'rhan samya

children.translated_text: [continuation]
[continuation]
[reference: Vajr, Vaidya 80]

children.text: ) draṣṭavyaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? yāni hi tāni bhagavan dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni tathāgatena bhāṣitāni, alakṣaṇāni tāni bhagavaṃstathāgatena bhāṣitāni | tenocyante dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇānīti ||
children.translated_text: "Why is that? Those thirty-two marks of a great person, <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s>—as non-marks (<s>alakṣaṇa</s>) have they been spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore they are called 'the thirty-two marks of a great person.'" ||

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—should the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), be seen by means of the thirty-two marks of a great person (<s>dvātriṃśat mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>)?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One should not be seen by means of the thirty-two marks of a great person." [continued]

body.text: bhagavānāha - yaśca khalu punaḥ subhūte strī vā puruṣo vā dine dine gaṅgānadīvālukāsamānātmabhāvān parityajet, evaṃ parityajan gaṅgānadīvālukāsamān kalpāṃstānātmabhāvān parityajet, yaśca ito dharmaparyāyadantaśaścatuṣpādikāmapi gāthāmudgṛhyaparebhyo deśayet saṃprakāśayet, ayameva tatonidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyādaprameyamasaṃkhyeyam || 13 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "If, <s>Subhūti</s>, some woman or man were to give up their own bodies (<s>ātmabhāva</s>) day after day, as many as the grains of sand in the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, and thus giving them up were to give up their bodies for as many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) as there are grains of sand in the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, and if someone else, having taken up from this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> even a single verse of four lines, were to teach and illuminate it for others—this one would thereby produce a far greater heap of merit (<s>puṇyaskandha</s>), immeasurable and incalculable." || 13 ||

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirdharmavegenāśrūṇi prāmuñcat | so 'śrūṇi pramṛjya bhagavantametadavocat - āścaryaṃ bhagavan, paramāścaryaṃ sugata, yāvadayaṃ dharmaparyāyastathāgatena bhāṣito 'grayānasaṃprasthitānāṃ sattvānāmarthāya, śreṣṭhayānasaṃprasthitānāmarthāya, yato me bhagavan jñānamutpannam | na mayā bhagavan jātvevaṃrūpo dharmaparyāyaḥ śrutapūrvaḥ | parameṇa te bhagavan āścaryeṇa samanvāgatā bodhisattvā bhaviṣyanti, ye iha sūtre bhāṣyamāṇe śrutvā bhūtasaṃjñāmutpādayiṣyanti | tatkasya hetoḥ? yā caiṣā bhagavan bhūtasaṃjñā, saiva abhūtasaṃjñā | tasmāttathāgato bhāṣatebhūtasaṃjñā bhḥtasaṃjñeti ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, moved by the force of the <s>Dharma</s>, shed tears. Wiping his tears, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "It is wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s>! It is most wonderful, <s>Sugata</s>, that this discourse on <s>Dharma</s> has been spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> for the benefit of beings who have set out on the foremost vehicle, for the benefit of beings who have set out on the supreme vehicle — from which knowledge has arisen in me. Never before, <s>Bhagavān</s>, have I heard such a discourse on <s>Dharma</s>. Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> will be endowed with the greatest wonder, <s>Bhagavān</s>, who, hearing this <s>sūtra</s> being spoken, will produce a true perception (<s>bhūtasaṃjñā</s>). Why is that? That which is a true perception, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is itself a non-perception (<s>abhūtasaṃjñā</s>). Therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s> speaks of 'true perception, true perception.'"

body.text: na mama bhagavan āścaryaṃ yadahamimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣyamāṇamavakalpayāmi adhimucye | ye 'pi te bhagavan sattvā bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani paścime kāle paścime samaye paścimāyāṃ pañcaśatyāṃ saddharmavipralope vartamāne, ye imaṃ bhagavan dharmaparyāyamudgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti, te paramāścaryeṇa samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti | api tu khalu punarbhagavan na teṣāmātmasaṃjñā pravartiṣyate, na sattvasaṃjñā na jīvasaṃjñā na pudgalasaṃjñā pravartiṣyate, nāpi teṣāṃ kācitsaṃjñā nāsaṃjñā pravartate | tatkasya hetoḥ? yā sā bhagavan ātmasaṃjñā, saivāsaṃjñā | yā sattvasaṃjñā jīvasaṃjñā pudgalasaṃjñā, saivāsaṃjñā | tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvasaṃjñāpagatā hi buddha bhagavantaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "It is no wonder to me, <s>Bhagavān</s>, that I understand and have faith in this discourse on <s>Dharma</s> as it is being spoken. But those beings who will exist in the future time, in the last period, in the last epoch, in the last five hundred years when the true <s>Dharma</s> is in decline — those, <s>Bhagavān</s>, who will take up this discourse on <s>Dharma</s>, master it, recite it, fully comprehend it, and explain it in detail to others — they will be endowed with the greatest wonder. Moreover, <s>Bhagavān</s>, no notion of self (<s>ātmasaṃjñā</s>) will arise in them, no notion of a being (<s>sattvasaṃjñā</s>), no notion of a life-force (<s>jīvasaṃjñā</s>), no notion of a person (<s>pudgalasaṃjñā</s>) will arise in them; neither will any perception nor non-perception arise in them. Why is that? That which is the notion of self, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is itself a non-notion. That which is the notion of a being, the notion of a life-force, the notion of a person — that is itself a non-notion. Why is that? The blessed <s>Buddhas</s> are those who have departed from all notions."

body.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - evametat subhūte, evametat | paramāścaryasamanvāgatāste sattvā bhaviṣyanti, ye iha subhūte sūtre bhāṣyamāṇe notrasiṣyanti na (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajr</s>, <s>Vaidya</s> 81

children.text: ) saṃtrasiṣyanti na saṃtrāsamāpatsyante | tatkasya hetoḥ? paramapāramiteyaṃ subhūte tathāgatena bhāṣitā yadutāpāramitā | yāṃ ca subhūte tathāgataḥ paramapāramitāṃ bhāṣate, tāmaparimāṇā api buddhā bhagavanto bhāṣante | tenocyante paramapāramiteti ||
children.translated_text: be terrified, will not fall into terror. Why is that? This, <s>Subhūti</s>, has been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be the supreme perfection (<s>paramapāramitā</s>), namely, non-perfection (<s>apāramitā</s>). And that which the <s>Tathāgata</s> declares as the supreme perfection, <s>Subhūti</s>, that is also declared by immeasurable blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. Therefore it is called the supreme perfection."

body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is. Those beings will be endowed with the greatest wonder who, when this <s>sūtra</s> is being spoken here, <s>Subhūti</s>, will not be frightened, will not

body.text: api tu khalu punaḥ subhute yā tathāgatasya kṣāntipāramitā, saiva apāramitā | tatkasya hetoḥ? yadā me subhūte kalirājā aṅgapratyaṅgamāṃsānyacchaitsīt, nāsīnme tasmin samaye ātmasaṃjñā vā sattvasaṃjñā vā jīvasaṃjñā vā pudgalasaṃjñā vā, nāpi me kācitsaṃjñā vā asaṃjñā vā babhūva | tatkasya hetoḥ? sacenme subhūte tasmin samaye ātmasaṃjñā abhaviṣyat, vyāpādasaṃjñāpi me tasmin samaye 'bhaviṣyat | sacetsattvasaṃjñā jīvasaṃjñā pudgalasaṃjñābhaviṣyat, vyāpādasaṃjñāpi me tasmin samaye 'bhaviṣyat | tatkasya hetoḥ? abhijānāmyahaṃ subhūte atīte 'dhvani pañca jātiśatāni yadahaṃ kṣāntivādī ṛṣirabhūvam | tatrāpi me nātmasaṃjñā babhūva, na sattvasaṃjñā, na jīvasaṃjñā, na pudgalasaṃjñā babhūva | tasmāttarhi subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvasaṃjñā vivarjayitvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayitavyam | na rūpapratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam, na śabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmapratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam, na dharmapratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam, nādharmapratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam, na kvacitpratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? yatpratiṣṭhitaṃ tadevāpratiṣṭhitam | tasmādeva tathāgato bhāṣate - apratiṣṭhitena bodhisattvena dānaṃ dātavyam | na rūpaśabdagandharasasparśadharmapratiṣṭhitena dānaṃ dātavyam ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is itself a non-perfection (<s>apāramitā</s>). For what reason? When, <s>Subhūti</s>, King <s>Kalī</s> cut off my limbs and flesh, at that time I had no perception of self (<s>ātmasaṃjñā</s>), no perception of a being (<s>sattvasaṃjñā</s>), no perception of a soul (<s>jīvasaṃjñā</s>), no perception of a person (<s>pudgalasaṃjñā</s>), nor did I have any perception or non-perception. For what reason? If, <s>Subhūti</s>, at that time I had had a perception of self, I would also have had a perception of malice (<s>vyāpādasaṃjñā</s>) at that time. If I had had a perception of a being, a perception of a soul, or a perception of a person, I would also have had a perception of malice at that time. For what reason? I remember, <s>Subhūti</s>, in the past, five hundred births ago, when I was the sage <s>Kṣāntivādin</s> (the Teacher of Patience). At that time too I had no perception of self, no perception of a being, no perception of a soul, no perception of a person. Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, having abandoned all perceptions, should generate the mind toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect enlightenment). One should not generate a mind that abides in form; one should not generate a mind that abides in sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental objects; one should not generate a mind that abides in <s>dharma</s>; one should not generate a mind that abides in non-<s>dharma</s>; one should not generate a mind that abides in anything whatsoever. For what reason? Because that which abides is itself non-abiding. Therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s> declares: a gift should be given by a <s>bodhisattva</s> who does not abide [in anything]; a gift should not be given while abiding in form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental objects. ||

body.text: api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvena evaṃrūpo dānaparityāgaḥ kartavyaḥ sarvasattvānāmarthāya | tatkasya hetoḥ? yā caiṣā subhūte sattvasaṃjñā, saiva asaṃjñā | ya evaṃ te sarvasattvāstathāgatena bhāṣitāsta eva asattvāḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? bhūtavādī subhūte tathāgataḥ, satyavādī tathāvādī ananyathāvādī tathāgataḥ, na vitathavādī tathāgataḥ ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> should practice the renunciation of giving (<s>dānaparityāga</s>) in this manner, for the benefit of all beings. For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the perception of a being (<s>sattvasaṃjñā</s>) is itself a non-perception (<s>asaṃjñā</s>). Those whom the <s>Tathāgata</s> has spoken of as 'all beings' are themselves non-beings (<s>asattva</s>). For what reason? Because the <s>Tathāgata</s> speaks truth (<s>bhūtavādī</s>), speaks reality (<s>satyavādī</s>), speaks things as they are (<s>tathāvādī</s>), speaks not otherwise (<s>ananyathāvādī</s>); the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not speak falsely (<s>vitathavādī</s>). ||

body.text: api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte yastathāgatena dharmo 'bhisaṃbuddho deśito nidhyātaḥ, na tatra satyaṃ na mṛṣā | tadyathāpi nāma subhūte puruṣo 'ndhakārapraviṣṭo na kiṃcidapi paśyet, evaṃ vastupatito bodhisattvo draṣṭavyo yo vastupatito dānaṃ parityajati | tadyathāpi nāma subhūte cakṣuṣmān puruṣaḥ prabhātāyāṃ rātrau sūrye 'bhyudgate nānavidhāni rūpāṇi paśyet, evamavastupatito bodhisattvo draṣṭavyo yo 'vastupatito dānaṃ parityajati ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>dharma</s> that has been fully awakened to, taught, and contemplated by the <s>Tathāgata</s> — therein is neither truth nor falsehood. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a person who has entered into darkness would see nothing whatsoever — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has fallen into [attachment to] objects (<s>vastupatita</s>) be regarded, one who gives a gift while fallen into objects. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a person with sight, when the night has brightened and the sun has risen, would see manifold forms — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has not fallen into objects be regarded, one who gives a gift without falling into objects. ||

body.text: api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte ye kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā imaṃ dharmaparyāyamudgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti, (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajracchedikā</s>, <s>Vaidya</s> edition, page 82]

children.text: ) jñātāste subhūte tathāgatena buddhajñānena, dṛṣṭāste subhūte tathāgatena buddhacakṣuṣā, buddhāste tathāgatena | sarve te subhūte sattvā aprameyamasaṃkhyeyaṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyanti pratigrahīṣyanti || 14 ||
children.translated_text: — they are known, <s>Subhūti</s>, by the <s>Tathāgata</s> through <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge; they are seen, <s>Subhūti</s>, by the <s>Tathāgata</s> through the <s>Buddha</s>-eye; they are understood by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. All those beings, <s>Subhūti</s>, will beget and receive an immeasurable, incalculable heap of merit (<s>puṇyaskandha</s>). || 14 ||

body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, those sons or daughters of good family who will take up, hold, recite, and master this <s>dharma</s>-discourse, and who will illuminate it in detail for others —

body.text: yaśca khalu punaḥ subhūte strī vā puruṣo vā purvāhṇakālasamaye gaṅgānadīvālukāsamānātmabhāvān parityajet, evaṃ madhyāhnakālasamaye gaṅgānadīvālukāsamānātmabhāvān parityajet, sāyāhnakālasamaye gaṅgānadīvālukāsamānātmabhāvān parityajet, anena paryāyeṇa bahūni kalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇyātmabhāvān parityajet, yaścemaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā na pratikṣipet, ayameva tatonidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyādaprameyamasaṃkhyeyam, kaḥ punarvādo yo likhitvā udgṛhṇīyāddhārayedvācayetparyavāpnuyāt, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayet ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, if a woman or man were to give up as many bodily existences (<s>ātmabhāva</s>) as there are grains of sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the morning time, and likewise give up as many bodily existences as there are grains of sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> at midday, and give up as many bodily existences as there are grains of sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the evening time, and by this method give up bodily existences for many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) — and if someone else, having heard this <s>dharma</s>-discourse, were not to reject it — this latter one would on that account produce a far greater heap of merit, immeasurable and incalculable. How much more so one who, having written it down, would take it up, hold it, recite it, master it, and illuminate it in detail for others! ||

body.text: api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte acintyo 'tulyo 'yaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ | ayaṃ ca subhūte dharmaparyāyastathāgatena bhāṣito 'grayānasaṃprasthitānāṃ sattvānāmarthāya, śreṣṭhayānasaṃprasthitānāṃ sattvānāmarthāya | ye imaṃ dharmaparyāyamudgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti, jñātāste subhūte tathāgatena buddhajñānena, dṛṣṭāste subhūte tathāgatena buddhacakṣuṣā, buddhāste tathāgatena | sarve te subhūte sattvā aprameyeṇa puṇyaskandhenāṃ samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti | acintyenātulyenāmāpyenāparimāṇena puṇyaskandhena samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti | sarve te subhūte sattvāḥ samāṃśena bodhiṃ dhārayiṣyanti vacayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti | tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi śakyaṃ subhūte ayaṃ dharmaparyāyo hīnādhimuktiakaiḥ sattvaiḥ śrotum, nātmadṛṣṭikairna sattvadṛṣṭikairna jīvadṛṣṭikairna pudgaladṛṣṭikaiḥ | nābodhisattvapratijñai sattvaiḥ śakyamayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ śrotuṃ vā udgrahītuṃ vā dhārayituṃ vā vācayituṃ vā paryavāptuṃ vā | nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, this <s>dharma</s>-discourse is inconceivable and incomparable. And this <s>dharma</s>-discourse, <s>Subhūti</s>, has been spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> for the benefit of beings who have set out on the foremost vehicle, for the benefit of beings who have set out on the supreme vehicle. Those who will take up this <s>dharma</s>-discourse, master it, recite it, fully comprehend it, and explain it in detail to others — they are known, <s>Subhūti</s>, by the <s>Tathāgata</s> through <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge; they are seen, <s>Subhūti</s>, by the <s>Tathāgata</s> through the <s>Buddha</s>-eye; they are understood by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. All those beings, <s>Subhūti</s>, will be endowed with an immeasurable heap of merit (<s>puṇyaskandha</s>). They will be endowed with an inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, and boundless heap of merit. All those beings, <s>Subhūti</s>, will bear, recite, and fully comprehend the <s>bodhi</s> (enlightenment) in equal measure. For what reason? It is not possible, <s>Subhūti</s>, for beings of inferior disposition to hear this <s>dharma</s>-discourse — not those holding the view of a self, not those holding the view of a being, not those holding the view of a life-force, not those holding the view of a person. Nor is it possible for beings who have not undertaken the <s>bodhisattva</s> vow to hear, take up, master, recite, or fully comprehend this <s>dharma</s>-discourse. Such a thing does not exist.

body.text: api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte yatra pṛthivīpradeśe idaṃ sūtraṃ prakaśayiṣyate, pūjanīyaḥ sa pṛthivīpradeśo bhaviṣyati sadevamānuṣāsurasya lokasya | vandanīyaḥ pradakṣiṇīyaśca sa pṛthivīpradeśo bhaviṣyati, caityabhūtaḥ sa pṛthivīpradeśo bhaviṣyati || 15 ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, whatever spot of earth where this <s>sūtra</s> will be revealed — that spot of earth will be worthy of worship by the world of gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. That spot of earth will be worthy of veneration and circumambulation; that spot of earth will become like a <s>caitya</s> (sacred shrine). || 15 ||

body.text: api tu ye te subhūte kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā imānevaṃrūpān sūtrāntānudgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti, yoniśaśca manasikariṣyanti, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti, te paribhūtā bhaviṣyanti, suparibhūtāśca bhaviṣyanti | tatkasya hetoḥ? yāni ca teṣāṃ subhūte sattvānāṃ paurvajanmikānyaśubhāni karmāṇi kṛtānyapāyasaṃvarta

children.translated_text: [continued]
[continued] (
[Vajr, Vaidya p. 83]

children.text: ) dṛṣṭa eva dharme paribhūtatayā tāni paurvajanmikānyaśubhāni karmāṇi kṣapayiṣyanti, buddhabodhiṃ cānuprāpsyanti ||
children.translated_text: by the very fact of being despised in this present life, those unwholesome actions of former births will be exhausted, and they will attain the enlightenment of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhabodhi</s>). ||

body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, those sons or daughters of good families who will take up <s>sūtras</s> of this kind, master them, recite them, fully comprehend them, attend to them wisely, and explain them in detail to others — they will be despised, thoroughly despised. For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, whatever unwholesome actions (<s>aśubha karma</s>) those beings committed in former births, which would lead to rebirth in states of misfortune (<s>apāya</s>),

body.text: abhijānāmyahaṃ subhūte atīte 'dhvanyasaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairasaṃkhyeyatarairdīpaṃkarasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pareṇa paratareṇa caturaśītibuddhakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇyabhūvan ye mayārāgitāḥ, ārāgya na virāgitāḥ | yacca mayā subhūte te buddhā bhagavanta ārāgitāḥ, ārāgya na virāgitāḥ, yacca paścime kāle paścime samaye paścimāyāṃ pañcaśatyāṃ saddharmavipralopakāle vartamāne imānevaṃrūpān sūtrāntānudgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti, asya khalu punaḥ subhūte puṇyaskandhasyāntikādasau paurvakaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ śatatamīmapi kalāṃ nopaiti, sahasratamīmapi śatasahasratamīmapi koṭimamipi koṭiśatatamīmapi koṭiśatasahasratamīmapi koṭiniyutaśatasahasratamīmapi | saṃkhyāmapi kalāmapi gaṇanāmapi upamāmapi upaniṣadamapi yāvadaupamyamapi na kṣamate ||
body.translated_text: I recall, <s>Subhūti</s>, in the past, in incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) — even more than incalculable — beyond [the time of] the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, there were eighty-four hundred-thousands of millions of <s>Buddhas</s> whom I served, and having served them, I did not turn away from them. Yet, <s>Subhūti</s>, although I served those blessed <s>Buddhas</s> and having served them did not turn away — compared with the heap of merit of those who, in the last time, the last period, the last five hundred years when the true <s>Dharma</s> is being destroyed, will take up <s>sūtras</s> of this kind, master them, recite them, fully comprehend them, and explain them in detail to others — indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, that former heap of merit does not reach even a hundredth part of this heap of merit, nor a thousandth, nor a hundred-thousandth, nor a ten-millionth, nor a hundred-millionth, nor a thousand-millionth, nor a ten-thousand-millionth. Neither number, nor fraction, nor reckoning, nor comparison, nor analogy, nor even any similitude whatsoever can match it.

body.text: sacetpunaḥ subhūte teṣāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ vā ahaṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ bhāṣeyam, yāvatte kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā tasmin samaye puṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyanti, pratigrahīṣyanti, unmādaṃ sattvā anuprāpnuyuścittavikṣepaṃ vā gaccheyuḥ | api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte acintyo 'tulyo 'yaṃ dharmaparyāyastathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ | asya acintya eva vipākaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyaḥ || 16 ||
body.translated_text: If, <s>Subhūti</s>, I were to declare the heap of merit of those sons or daughters of good families — the heap of merit that those sons or daughters of good families will produce and receive at that time — beings would go mad or fall into mental distraction. Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, this <s>dharma</s>-discourse is inconceivable and incomparable, spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. An inconceivable fruit (<s>vipāka</s>) is to be expected from it. || 16 ||

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - kathaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvayānasaṃprasthitena sthātavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam, kathaṃ cittaṃ pragrahītavyam? bhagavānāha - iha subhūte bodhisattvayānasaṃprasthitena evaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam - sarve sattvā mayā anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāpayitavyāḥ | evaṃ sa sattvān parinirvāpya na kaścitsattvaḥ parinirvāpito bhavati | tatkasya hetoḥ? sacetsubhūte bodhisattvasya sattvasaṃjñā pravarteta, na sa bodhisattva iti vaktavyaḥ | jīvasaṃjñā vā yāvatpudgalasaṃjñā vā pravarteta, na sa bodhisattva iti vaktavyaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? nāsti subhūte sa kaściddharmo yo bodhisattvayānasaṃprasthito nāma ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "How, <s>Bhagavān</s>, should one who has set out on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle stand? How should one practice? How should one control the mind?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, one who has set out on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle should produce this thought: 'All beings should be led by me to <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the realm of <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>anupadhiśeṣa nirvāṇadhātu</s>).' Yet even having thus led beings to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, no being whatsoever has been led to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. For what reason? If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the notion of a being (<s>sattvasaṃjñā</s>) were to arise in a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, he should not be called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. If the notion of a life-force (<s>jīvasaṃjñā</s>), or even the notion of a person (<s>pudgalasaṃjñā</s>), were to arise, he should not be called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. For what reason? There is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever, <s>Subhūti</s>, that is called 'one who has set out on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle.'

children.translated_text: <s>Vajracchedikā</s>, <s>Vaidya</s> [edition, page] 84

children.text: ) tatkiṃ manyase subhūte asti sa kaściddharmo yastathāgatena dīpaṃkarasya tathāgatasyāntikādanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ? evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - yathāhaṃ bhagavato bhāṣitasyārthamājānāmi, nāsti sa bhagavan kaściddharmo yastathāgatena dīpaṃkarasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntikādanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ | evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocat - evametatsubhūte, evametat | nāsti subhūte sa kaściddharmo yastathāgatena dīpaṃkarasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntikādanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ | sacetpunaḥ subhūte kaściddharmastathāgatenābhisaṃbuddho 'bhaviṣyat, na māṃ dīpaṃkarastathāgato vyākariṣyat - bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇava anāgate 'dhvani śākyamunirnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha iti | yasmāttarhi subhūte tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena nāsti sa kaściddharmo yo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ, tasmādahaṃ dīpaṃkareṇa tathāgatena vyākṛta - bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇava anāgate 'dhvani śākyamunirnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathāgata iti subhūte bhūtatathatāyā etadadhivacanam | tathāgata iti subhūte anutpādadharmatāyā etadadhivacanam | tathāgata iti subhūte dharmocchedasyaitadadhivacanam | tathāgata iti subhūte atyantānutpannasyaitadadhivacanam | tatkasya hetoḥ? eṣa subhūte anutpādo yaḥ paramārthaḥ | yaḥ kaścitsubhūte evaṃ vadet - tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddheti, sa vitathaṃ vadet | abhyācakṣīta māṃ sa subhūte asatodgṛhītena | tatkasya hetoḥ -? nāsti subhūte sa kaściddharmo yastathāgatena anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ | yaśca subhūte tathāgatena dharmo 'bhisaṃbuddho deśito vā tatra na satyaṃ na mṛṣā | tasmāttathāgato bhāṣate - sarvadharmā buddhadharmā iti | tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvadharmā iti subhūte adharmāstathāgatena bhāṣitāḥ | tasmāducyante sarvadharmā buddhadharmā iti ||
children.translated_text: ) What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — is there any <s>dharma</s> that the <s>Tathāgata</s> fully awakened to as <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect enlightenment) in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>? Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: As I understand the meaning of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, there is no <s>dharma</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, that the <s>Tathāgata</s> fully awakened to as <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is. There is no <s>dharma</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, that the <s>Tathāgata</s> fully awakened to as <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. If, moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, any <s>dharma</s> had been fully awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, then the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṅkara</s> would not have given the prediction: 'You, young man, will in the future become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One by the name of <s>Śākyamuni</s>.' Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has fully awakened to as <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, therefore I was given the prediction by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>: 'You, young man, will in the future become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One by the name of <s>Śākyamuni</s>.' For what reason? '<s>Tathāgata</s>' (<s>Thus-Gone</s>), <s>Subhūti</s>, is a synonym for true suchness (<s>bhūtatathatā</s>). '<s>Tathāgata</s>,' <s>Subhūti</s>, is a synonym for the nature of non-arising (<s>anutpādadharmatā</s>). '<s>Tathāgata</s>,' <s>Subhūti</s>, is a synonym for the cutting off of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmoccheda</s>). '<s>Tathāgata</s>,' <s>Subhūti</s>, is a synonym for that which has utterly never arisen (<s>atyantānutpanna</s>). For what reason? This non-arising, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>). If anyone, <s>Subhūti</s>, were to say, 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has fully awakened to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>,' he would speak falsely. He would misrepresent me, <s>Subhūti</s>, by seizing upon what is untrue. For what reason? There is no <s>dharma</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, that the <s>Tathāgata</s> has fully awakened to as <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. And whatever <s>dharma</s> the <s>Tathāgata</s> has awakened to or taught — in it there is neither truth nor falsehood. Therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s> speaks thus: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>.' For what reason? All <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, have been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be non-<s>dharmas</s>. Therefore they are called all <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>.

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma subhūte puruṣo bhavedupetakāyo mahākāyaḥ? āyuṣmān subhūtirāha - yo 'sau bhagavaṃstathāgatena puruṣo bhāṣita upetakāyo mahākāya iti, akāyaḥ sa bhagavaṃstathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ | tenocyate upetakāyo mahākāya iti ||
body.translated_text: Suppose, <s>Subhūti</s>, there were a person endowed with a body, a great body? The venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said: That person, <s>Bhagavān</s>, whom the <s>Tathāgata</s> has called 'endowed with a body, a great body' — he has been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be without a body (<s>akāya</s>). Therefore he is called 'endowed with a body, a great body.'

body.text: bhagavānāha - evametatsubhūte | yo bodhisattva evaṃ vadet - ahaṃ sattvān parinirvāpayiṣyāmiti, na sa bodhisattva iti vaktavyaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? asti subhūte sa kaściddharmo yo bodhisattvo nāma? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | nāsti sa kaściddharmo yo bodhisattvo (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajr</s>, <s>Vaidya</s> 85

children.text: ) nāma | bhagavānāha - sattvāḥ sattvā iti subhūte asattvāste tathāgatena bhāṣitāḥ, tenocyante sattvā iti | tasmāttathāgato bhāṣate - nirātmānaḥ sarvadharmā nirjīvā niṣpoṣā niṣpudgalāḥ sarvadharmā iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "'Beings, beings,' <s>Subhūti</s> — they have been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be non-beings; therefore they are called 'beings.' Therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s> declares: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are without self (<s>nirātman</s>), all <s>dharmas</s> are without a life-force (<s>nirjīva</s>), without a nourisher (<s>niṣpoṣa</s>), without a person (<s>niṣpudgala</s>).'"

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>. Whatever <s>bodhisattva</s> were to say, 'I shall lead beings to <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — he should not be called a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Why is that? Is there, <s>Subhūti</s>, any <s>dharma</s> (entity) called '<s>bodhisattva</s>'?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. There is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever called '<s>bodhisattva</s>'"

body.text: yaḥ subhūte bodhisattva evaṃ vadet - ahaṃ kṣetravyūhānniṣpādayiṣyāmīti, sa vitathaṃ vadet | tatkasya hetoḥ? kṣetravyūhāḥ kṣetravyūhā iti subhūte avyūhāste tathāgatena bhāṣitāḥ | tenocyante kṣetravyūhā iti ||
body.translated_text: "Whatever <s>bodhisattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, were to say, 'I shall bring about the adornment of buddha-fields (<s>kṣetravyūha</s>)' — he would speak falsely. Why is that? 'The adornments of buddha-fields, the adornments of buddha-fields,' <s>Subhūti</s> — they have been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be non-adornments; therefore they are called 'adornments of buddha-fields.'"

body.text: yaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo nirātmāno dharmā nirātmāno dharmā ityadhimucyate, tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena bodhisattvo mahāsattva ityākhyātaḥ || 17 ||
body.translated_text: "Whatever <s>bodhisattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, has conviction that '<s>dharmas</s> are without self, <s>dharmas</s> are without self' — that one has been designated by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, as a '<s>bodhisattva</s>, a great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>).'" || 17 ||

body.text: bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte - saṃvidyate tathāgatasya māṃsacakṣuḥ? subhūtirāha - evametadbhagavan, saṃvidyate tathāgatasya māṃsacakṣuḥ | bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte saṃvidyate tathāgatasya divyaṃ cakṣuḥ? subhūtirāha - evametadbhagavan, saṃvidyate tathāgatasya divyaṃ cakṣuḥ | bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte saṃvidyate tathāgatasya prajñācakṣuḥ? subhūtirāha - evametadbhagavan, saṃvidyate tathāgatasya prajñācakṣuḥ | bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte saṃvidyate tathāgatasya dharmacakṣuḥ? subhūtirāha - evametadbhagavan, saṃvidyate tathāgatasya dharmacakṣuḥ | bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte saṃvidyate tathāgatasya buddhacakṣuḥ? subhūtirāha - evametadbhagavan, saṃvidyate tathāgata buddhacakṣuḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — does the <s>Tathāgata</s> possess the fleshly eye (<s>māṃsacakṣus</s>)?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "So it is, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> possesses the fleshly eye." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — does the <s>Tathāgata</s> possess the divine eye (<s>divyacakṣus</s>)?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "So it is, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> possesses the divine eye." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — does the <s>Tathāgata</s> possess the wisdom eye (<s>prajñācakṣus</s>)?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "So it is, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> possesses the wisdom eye." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — does the <s>Tathāgata</s> possess the <s>Dharma</s> eye (<s>dharmacakṣus</s>)?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "So it is, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> possesses the <s>Dharma</s> eye." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — does the <s>Tathāgata</s> possess the <s>Buddha</s> eye (<s>buddhacakṣus</s>)?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "So it is, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> possesses the <s>Buddha</s> eye."

body.text: bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yāvantyo gaṅgāyāṃ mahānadyāṃ vālukāḥ, api nu tā vālukāstathāgatena bhāṣitāḥ? subhūtirāha - evametadbhagavan, evametat sugata | bhāṣitāstathāgatena vālukāḥ | bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yāvatyo gaṅgāyāṃ mahānadyāṃ vālukāḥ, tāvatya eva gaṅgānadyo bhaveyuḥ, tāsu vā vālukāḥ, tāvantaśca lokadhātavo bhaveyuḥ, kaccidbahavaste lokadhātavo bhaveyuḥ? subhūtirāha - evametadbhagavan, evametat sugata | bahavaste lokadhātavo bhaveyuḥ | bhagavānāha - yāvantaḥ subhūte teṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvāḥ, teṣāmahaṃ nānābhāvāṃ cittadhārāṃ prajānāmi | tatkasya hetoḥ? cittadhārā cittadhāreti subhūte adhāraiṣā tathāgatena bhāṣitā, tenocyate cittadhāreti | tatkasya hetoḥ? atītaṃ subhūte cittaṃ nopalabhyate | anāgataṃ cittaṃ nopalabhyate | pratyutpannaṃ cittaṃ nopalabhyate || 18 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — the grains of sand in the great river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, have they been spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as grains of sand?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "So it is, <s>Bhagavān</s>, so it is, <s>Sugata</s>. They have been spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as grains of sand." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — if there were as many <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers as there are grains of sand in the great river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and as many world-systems (<s>lokadhātu</s>) as there are grains of sand in those [rivers], would those world-systems be many?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "So it is, <s>Bhagavān</s>, so it is, <s>Sugata</s>.
