body.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte yaḥ kaścitkulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ saptaratnaparipūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tathāgatebhyo 'rhadbhayaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyo dānaṃ dadyāt, api nu (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajr</s>, <s>Vaidya</s> 86

children.text: ) sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyāt? subhūtirāha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata | bhagavānāha - evametatsubhūte, evametat | bahu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyādaprameyamasaḥkhyeyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? puṇyaskandhaḥ puṇyaskandha iti subhūte askandhaḥ sa tathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ | tenocyate puṇyaskandha iti | sacet punaḥ subhūte puṇyaskandho 'bhaviṣyat, na tathāgato 'bhāṣiṣyat puṇyaskandhaḥ puṇyaskandha iti || 19 ||
children.translated_text: Would that son or daughter of good family thereby produce a great heap of merit (<s>puṇyaskandha</s>)?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Great indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Great indeed, <s>Sugata</s>!" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is. That son or daughter of good family would thereby produce a great heap of merit, immeasurable and incalculable. Why is that? That heap of merit, <s>Subhūti</s>—as a non-heap (<s>askandha</s>) has it been spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore it is called 'a heap of merit.' If, <s>Subhūti</s>, there were [truly] a heap of merit, the <s>Tathāgata</s> would not have spoken of 'a heap of merit, a heap of merit.'" || 19 ||

body.translated_text: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — if a son or daughter of good family were to fill this three-thousand-great-thousand world-system (<s>trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>) with the seven precious things and offer it as a gift to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones, would

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte rūpakāyapariniṣpattyā tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | na rūpakāyapariniṣpattyā tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? rūpakāyapariniṣpattī rūpakāyapariniṣpattiriti bhagavan apariniṣpattireṣā tathāgatena bhāṣitā | tenocyate rūpakāyapariniṣpattiriti ||
body.translated_text: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—should the <s>Tathāgata</s> be seen through the perfection of the form-body (<s>rūpakāyapariniṣpatti</s>)?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s> should not be seen through the perfection of the form-body. Why is that? That perfection of the form-body, <s>Bhagavān</s>—as a non-perfection (<s>apariniṣpatti</s>) has it been spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore it is called 'the perfection of the form-body.'" ||

body.text: bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte lakṣaṇasaṃpadā tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavān | na lakṣaṇasaṃpadā tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? yaiṣā bhagavan lakṣaṇasaṃpattathāgatena bhāṣitā, alakṣaṇasaṃpadeṣā tathāgatena bhāṣitā | tenocyate lakṣaṇasaṃpaditi || 20 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—should the <s>Tathāgata</s> be seen through the possession of marks (<s>lakṣaṇasaṃpad</s>)?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s> should not be seen through the possession of marks. Why is that? That possession of marks, <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s>—as a possession of non-marks (<s>alakṣaṇasaṃpad</s>) has it been spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore it is called 'the possession of marks.'" || 20 ||

body.text: bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ manyase subhūte api nu tathāgatasyaivaṃ bhavati - mayā dharmo deśita iti? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan tathāgatasyaivaṃ bhavati - mayā dharmo deśita iti | bhagavānāha - yaḥ subhūte evaṃ vadet - tathāgatena dharmo deśita iti, sa vitathaṃ vadet | abhyācakṣīta māṃ sa subhūte asatodgṛhītena | tatkasya hetoḥ? dharmadeśanā dharmadeśaneti subhūte nāsti sa kaściddharmo yo dharmadeśanā nāmopalabhyate ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—does the <s>Tathāgata</s> think: 'A <s>dharma</s> has been taught by me'?" <s>Subhūti</s> said: "No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s> does not think: 'A <s>dharma</s> has been taught by me.'" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Whoever, <s>Subhūti</s>, would say 'A <s>dharma</s> has been taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'—he would speak falsely. He would misrepresent me, <s>Subhūti</s>, by grasping what is not so. Why is that? '<s>Dharmadeśanā</s>, <s>dharmadeśanā</s> (teaching of dharma)'—<s>Subhūti</s>, there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that can be apprehended as a 'teaching of dharma.'" ||

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirbhagavantametadavocat - asti bhagavan kecitsattvā bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani paścime kāle paścime samaye paścimāyāṃ pañcaśatyāṃ saddharmavipralope vartamāne, ya imānevaṃrūpān dharmān śrutvā abhiśraddhāsyanti | bhagavānāha - na te subhūte sattvā nāsattvāḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? sattvāḥ sattvā iti subhūte sarve te subhūte asattvāstathāgatena bhāṣitāḥ | tenocyante sattvā iti || 21 ||
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "<s>Bhagavān</s>, will there be any beings in the future time, in the last period, in the last epoch, in the last five hundred years when the true <s>dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>) is disappearing, who, hearing such <s>dharmas</s> as these, will have faith in them?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "They are neither beings nor non-beings, <s>Subhūti</s>. Why is that? 'Beings, beings,' <s>Subhūti</s>—all of them have been spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as non-beings. Therefore they are called 'beings.'" || 21 ||

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte - api nu asti sa kaściddharmaḥ, yastathāgatenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ?@ āyuṣmān subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | nāsti sa bhagavan kaściddharmo yastathāgatenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ | bhagavānāha - evametatsubhūte, evametat | aṇurapi tatra dharmo na saṃvidyate nopalabhyate | tenocyate anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiriti || 22 ||
body.translated_text: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>—is there any <s>dharma</s> by which the <s>Tathāgata</s> has fully awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)?" The venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said: "No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. There is no <s>dharma</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, by which the <s>Tathāgata</s> has fully awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is. Not even the slightest <s>dharma</s> is found or apprehended therein. Therefore it is called 'the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.'" || 22 ||

children.translated_text: [reference: Vajr, Vaidya 87]

children.text: ) api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte samaḥ sa dharmo na tatra kaścidviṣamaḥ | tenocyate anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiriti | nirātmatvena niḥsattvatvena nirjīvatvena niṣpudgalatvena samā sā anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ sarvaiḥ kuśalairdharmairabhisaṃbudhyate | tatkasya hetoḥ? kuśalā dharmāḥ kuśalā dharmā iti subhūte adharmāścaiva te tathāgatena bhāṣitāḥ | tenocyante kuśalā dharmā iti || 23 ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, that <s>dharma</s> is equal (<s>sama</s>); there is nothing unequal in it. Therefore it is called 'the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.' Through the absence of self (<s>nirātmatva</s>), the absence of a being (<s>niḥsattvatva</s>), the absence of a life-force (<s>nirjīvatva</s>), and the absence of a person (<s>niṣpudgalatva</s>), that unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is equal, and it is fully awakened to through all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (<s>kuśala dharma</s>). Why is that? 'Wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, wholesome <s>dharmas</s>'—<s>Subhūti</s>, as non-<s>dharmas</s> (<s>adharma</s>) have they been spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore they are called 'wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.'" || 23 ||

body.translated_text: [page break]

body.text: yaśca khalu punaḥ subhute strī vā puruṣo vā yāvantastrisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sumeravaḥ parvatarājānaḥ, tāvato rāśīn saptānāṃ ratnānāmabhisaṃhṛtya tathāgatebhyo 'rhadbhayaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyo dānaṃ dadyāt, yaśca kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā itaḥ prajñāpāramitāyā dharmaparyāyādantaśaścatuṣpādikāmapi gāthāmudgṛhya parebhyo deśayet, asya subhūte puṇyaskandhasya asau paurvakaḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ śatatamīmapi kalāṃ nopaiti, yāvadupaniṣadamapi na kṣamate || 24 ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, if a woman or a man were to gather heaps of the seven precious things, as many as there are <s>Sumeru</s> mountain kings in the trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>), and give them as a gift to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones; and if a son or daughter of good family were to take up from this <s>Prajñāpāramitā dharma</s>-discourse even a single verse of four lines and teach it to others — this heap of merit, <s>Subhūti</s>, compared to the former heap of merit, would not reach even a hundredth part, nor even bear comparison. || 24 ||

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte - api nu tathāgatasyaivaṃ bhavati - mayā sattvāḥ parimocitā iti? na khalu punaḥ subhūte evaṃ draṣṭavyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? nāsti subhūte kaścitsattvo yastathāgatena parimocitaḥ | yadi punaḥ subhūte kaścitsattvo 'bhaviṣyadyastathāgatena parimocitaḥ syāt, sa eva tathāgatasyātmagrāho 'bhaviṣyat, sattvagrāho jīvagrāhaḥ pudgalagrāho 'bhaviṣyat | ātmagrāha iti subhūte agrāha eṣa tathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ | sa ca bālapṛthagjanairudgṛhītaḥ | bālapṛthagjanā iti subhūte ajanā eva te tathāgatena bhāṣitāḥ | tenocyante bālapṛthagjanā iti || 25 ||
body.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — does this thought arise in the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'Beings have been liberated by me'? That is not so, <s>Subhūti</s>; it should not be viewed thus. For what reason? There is no being whatsoever, <s>Subhūti</s>, who has been liberated by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, there had been any being who had been liberated by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, that itself would have been the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s grasping at a self (<s>ātmagrāha</s>), grasping at a being (<s>sattvagrāha</s>), grasping at a soul (<s>jīvagrāha</s>), grasping at a person (<s>pudgalagrāha</s>). Grasping at a self, <s>Subhūti</s>, has been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be a non-grasping (<s>agrāha</s>). Yet it is grasped by foolish ordinary persons (<s>bālapṛthagjana</s>). Foolish ordinary persons, <s>Subhūti</s>, have been declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be non-persons (<s>ajana</s>). Therefore they are called foolish ordinary persons. || 25 ||

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase subhūte - lakṣaṇasaṃpadā tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | yathāhaṃ bhagavato bhāṣitasyārthamājānāmi, na lakṣaṇasaṃpadā tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ | bhagavānāha - sādhu sādhu subhūte, evametatsubhūte, evametadyathā vadasi | na lakṣaṇasaṃpadā tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? sacetpunaḥ subhūte lakṣaṇasaṃpadā tathāgato draṣṭavyo 'bhaviṣyat, rājāpi cakravartī tathāgato 'bhaviṣyat | tasmānna lakṣaṇasaṃpadā tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ | āyuṣmān subhutirbhagavantametadavocat - yathāhaṃ bhagavato bhāṣitasyārthamājānāmi, na lakṣaṇasaṃpadā tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — should the <s>Tathāgata</s> be seen through the perfection of marks (<s>lakṣaṇasaṃpad</s>)? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. As I understand the meaning of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, the <s>Tathāgata</s> should not be seen through the perfection of marks. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Well said, well said, <s>Subhūti</s>! So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, it is just as you say. The <s>Tathāgata</s> should not be seen through the perfection of marks. For what reason? If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> were to be seen through the perfection of marks, then even a universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>) would be a <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s> should not be seen through the perfection of marks. The venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: As I understand the meaning of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, the <s>Tathāgata</s> should not be seen through the perfection of marks. ||

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmime gāthe abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then at that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke these verses:

children.text: ye māṃ rūpeṇa cādrākṣurye māṃ ghoṣeṇa cānvaguḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who saw me through form, and those who followed me through sound —

children.text: mithyāprahāṇaprasṛtā na māṃ drakṣyanti te janāḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: They have set forth on a wrong path; those people will not see me. || 1 ||

body.text:
dharmato buddho draṣṭavyo dharmakāyā hi nāyakāḥ |
dharmatā ca na vijñeyā na sā śakyā vijānitum || 2 || 26 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> should be seen through the <s>Dharma</s>, for the guides [of the world] have the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body) as their body. And the true nature of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmatā</s>) cannot be discerned; it is not possible to know it. || 2 || 26 ||

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajracchedikā</s>, <s>Vaidya</s> edition, page 88]

children.text: ) tatkiṃ manyase subhūte lakṣaṇasaṃpadā tathāgatena anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddhā? na khalu punaste subhūte evaṃ draṣṭavyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi subhūte lakṣaṇasaṃpadā tathāgatena anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddhā syāt | na khalu punaste subhūte kaścidevaṃ vadet - bodhisattvayānasaṃprasthitaiḥ kasyaciddharmasya vināśaḥ prajñaptaḥ ucchedo veti | na khalu punaste subhūte evaṃ draṣṭavyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? na bodhisattvayānasaṃprasthitaiḥ kasyaciddharmasya vināśaḥ prajñapto nocchedaḥ || 27 ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — was <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect enlightenment) realized by the <s>Tathāgata</s> through the perfection of marks? That should not be viewed thus, <s>Subhūti</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> could not have realized <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> through the perfection of marks. Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, let no one say this: 'By those who have set out on the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle, the destruction or annihilation of any <s>dharma</s> has been proclaimed.' That should not be viewed thus, <s>Subhūti</s>. For what reason? By those who have set out on the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle, neither the destruction nor the annihilation of any <s>dharma</s> has been proclaimed. || 27 ||

body.text: yaśca khalu punaḥ subhūte kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāṃllokadhātūn saptaratnaparipūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tathāgatebhyo 'rhadbhayaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyo dānaṃ dadyāt, yaśca bodhisattvo nirātmakeṣvanutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntiṃ pratilabhate, ayameva tatonidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavedaprameyamasaṃkhyeyam | na khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena puṇyaskandhaḥ parigrahītavyaḥ | āyuṣmān subhūtirāha - nanu bhagavan bodhisattvena puṇyaskandhaḥ parigrahītavyaḥ? bhagavānāha - parigrahītavyaḥ subhūte no grahītavyaḥ | tenocyate parigrahītavya iti || 28 ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, if a son or daughter of good family were to fill as many world-systems as there are grains of sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> with the seven precious things and give them as a gift to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones; and if a <s>bodhisattva</s> were to attain patient acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>) with regard to <s>dharmas</s> that are selfless (<s>nirātmaka</s>) and unarisen (<s>anutpattika</s>) — this latter one would thereby produce a far greater heap of merit, immeasurable and incalculable. Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, a heap of merit should not be appropriated by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. The venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said: Should not a heap of merit be appropriated by a <s>bodhisattva</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: It should be appropriated, <s>Subhūti</s>, but not grasped. Therefore it is said 'to be appropriated.' || 28 ||

body.text: api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte yaḥ kaścidevaṃ vadet - tathāgato gacchati vā āgacchati vā tiṣṭhati vā niṣīdati vā, śayyāṃ vā kalpayati, na me subhūte (sa) bhāṣitasyārthamājānāti | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathāgata iti subhūte ucyate na kvacidgato na kutaścidāgataḥ | tenocyate tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha iti || 29 ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, whoever would say: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> goes, or comes, or stands, or sits, or reclines' — that person, <s>Subhūti</s>, does not understand the meaning of what I have spoken. For what reason? The one who is called '<s>Tathāgata</s>,' <s>Subhūti</s>, has not gone anywhere nor come from anywhere. Therefore he is called the <s>Tathāgata</s> (the Thus-Gone/Thus-Come One), the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. || 29 ||

body.text: yaśca khalu punaḥ subhūte kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā yāvanti trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau pṛthivīrajāṃsi, tāvatāṃ lokadhātūnāmevaṃrūpaṃ maṣiṃ kuryāt yāvadevamasaṃkhyeyena vīryeṇa tadyathāpi nāma paramāṇusaṃcayaḥ, tatkiṃ manyase subhūte - api nu bahuḥ sa paramāṇusaṃcayo bhavet? subhūtirāha - evametadbhagavan, evametatsugata | bahuḥ sa paramāṇusaṃcayo bhavet | tatkasya hetoḥ? sacedbhagavan bahuḥ paramāṇusaṃcayo 'bhaviṣyat, na bhagavānavakṣyat - paramāṇusaṃcaya iti | tatkasya hetoḥ? yo 'sau bhagavan paramāṇusaṃcayastathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ, asaṃcayaḥ sa tathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ | tenocyate paramāṇusaṃcaya iti | yaśca tathāgatena bhāṣitastrisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturiti, adhātuḥ sa tathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ | tenocyate trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturiti | tatkasya hetoḥ? sacedbhagavan lokadhāturabhaviṣyat, sa eva piṇḍagrāho (

children.translated_text: [Vajr, Vaidya p. 89]

children.text: ) 'bhaviṣyat | yaścaiva piṇḍagrāhastathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ, agrāhaḥ sa tathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ | tenocyate piṇḍagrāha iti | bhagavānāha - piṇḍagrāhaścaiva subhūte avyavahāro 'nabhilāpyaḥ | na sa dharmo nādharmaḥ | sa ca bālapṛthagjanairudgṛhītaḥ || 30 ||
children.translated_text: And that which the <s>Tathāgata</s> has called a solid mass grasping — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared it to be a non-grasping. Therefore it is called a "solid mass grasping."' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'And a solid mass grasping, <s>Subhūti</s>, is itself an inexpressible convention (<s>avyavahāra</s>), beyond words. It is neither <s>dharma</s> nor non-<s>dharma</s>. And yet it has been seized upon by childish ordinary persons (<s>bālapṛthagjana</s>).' || 30 ||

body.translated_text: And again, <s>Subhūti</s>, if a son or daughter of good family were to take as many dust particles as there are in this trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>), and of those many world-systems were to make an ink-like mass with immeasurable effort, just as it were an accumulation of atoms (<s>paramāṇusaṃcaya</s>) — what do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, would that accumulation of atoms be great? <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'So it is, <s>Bhagavān</s>; so it is, <s>Sugata</s>. That accumulation of atoms would be great. For what reason? If, <s>Bhagavān</s>, that had been a great accumulation of atoms, the <s>Bhagavān</s> would not have called it an "accumulation of atoms." For what reason? That which the <s>Bhagavān</s> has called an accumulation of atoms, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared to be a non-accumulation. Therefore it is called an "accumulation of atoms." And the trichiliocosm spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s> — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared it to be a non-world-system (<s>adhātu</s>). Therefore it is called "a trichiliocosm." For what reason? If, <s>Bhagavān</s>, there had been a world-system, that itself would have been a solid mass grasping (<s>piṇḍagrāha</s>)

body.text: tatkasya hetoḥ? yo hi kaścitsubhūte evaṃ vadet - ātmadṛṣṭistathāgatena bhāṣitā, sattvadṛṣṭirjīvadṛṣṭiḥ pudgaladṛṣṭistathāgatena bhāṣitā, api nu sa subhūte samyagvadamāno vadet? subhūtirāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan, no hīdaṃ sugata, na samyagvadamāno vadet | tatkasya hetoḥ? yā sā bhagavan ātmadṛṣṭistathāgatena bhāṣitā, adṛṣṭiḥ sā tathāgatena bhāṣitā | tenocyate ātmadṛṣṭiriti ||
body.translated_text: For what reason? If, <s>Subhūti</s>, anyone were to say: 'A view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) has been spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, a view of a being, a view of a life-force, a view of a person has been spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s>' — would that person, <s>Subhūti</s>, be speaking correctly? <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>; no indeed, <s>Sugata</s> — he would not be speaking correctly. For what reason? That which, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has spoken of as a view of self — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared it to be a non-view (<s>adṛṣṭi</s>). Therefore it is called a "view of self."'

body.text: bhagavānāha - evaṃ hi subhūte bodhisattvayānasaṃprasthitena sarvadharmā jñātavyā draṣṭavyā adhimoktavyāḥ | tathāca jñātavyā draṣṭavyā adhimoktavyāḥ, yathā na dharmasaṃjñāyāmapi pratyupatiṣṭhennādharmasaṃjñāyām | tatkasya hetoḥ? dharmasaṃjñā dharmasaṃjñeti subhūte asaṃjñaiṣā tathāgatena bhāṣitā | tenocyate dharmasaṃjñeti || 31 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, one who has set out on the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle should know, see, and have faith in all <s>dharmas</s>. And one should know, see, and have faith in them in such a way that one does not take one's stand even on the perception of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmasaṃjñā</s>), nor on the perception of non-<s>dharma</s>. For what reason? The perception of <s>dharma</s>, the perception of <s>dharma</s>, <s>Subhūti</s> — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared it to be a non-perception (<s>asaṃjñā</s>). Therefore it is called the "perception of <s>dharma</s>."' || 31 ||

body.text: yaśca khalu punaḥ subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'prameyānasaṃkhyeyāṃllokadhātūn saptaratnaparipūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tathāgatebhyo 'rhadbhayaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyo dānaṃ dadyāt, yaśca kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā itaḥ prajñāpāramitāyā dharmaparyāyādantaśaścatuṣpādikāmapi gāthāmudgṛhya dhārayeddeśayedvācayet paryavāpnuyāt, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayet, ayameva tatonidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyādaprameyamasaṃkhyeyam | kathaṃ ca saṃprakāśayet? tadyathākāśe -
body.translated_text: And if, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> were to fill immeasurable and incalculable world-systems with the seven precious things and give them as a gift to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones, and if a son or daughter of good family were to take up from this <s>Prajñāpāramitā dharma</s>-discourse even a single verse of four lines and master it, teach it, recite it, fully comprehend it, and explain it in detail to others — this [latter] one would on that account produce a far greater heap of merit, immeasurable and incalculable. And how should one illuminate it? As if in space —

children.translated_text: Stars, a fault of vision, a lamp, an illusion, dew, a bubble,

children.text: svapnaṃ ca vidyudabhraṃ ca evaṃ draṣṭavya saṃskṛtam ||
children.translated_text: a dream, a lightning flash, and a cloud — thus should one view all conditioned things (<s>saṃskṛta</s>). ||

body.text: tathā prakāśayet, tenocyate saṃprakāśayediti ||
body.translated_text: Thus should one illuminate it; therefore it is said, 'one should illuminate it.' ||

body.text: idamavocadbhagavān āttamanāḥ | sthavirasubhūtiste ca bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāste ca bodhisattvāḥ sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti || 32 ||
body.translated_text: This the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke, and the delighted elder <s>Subhūti</s>, those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, and those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and the whole world with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. || 32 ||

body.text: || āryavajracchedikā bhagavatī prajñāpāramitā samāptā ||
body.translated_text: || The Noble <s>Vajracchedikā</s>, the Blessed <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, is complete. ||
